transcript_raw:
Participant: P01 | Session 1 | GTA V | minimal HUD | Interviewer: Researcher 2
[00:00] Interviewer: Okay [name], thanks. Let's start the interview for session 1.
[00:10] Interviewer: Q1. How did you figure out where to go during the session? What did you look at or rely on?
[00:14] P01: um, like, [silence 4s] I had to use like, landmarks like the tall buildings and signs.
[00:51] Interviewer: Q2. Were there moments when something on the screen confused you? What was happening?
[00:56] P01: ahh, like, I was not you know, sure where the objective was. Like I said, I'm [participant], I play this at home.
[01:32] Interviewer: Q3. Which HUD elements, if any, pulled your attention away from what you were doing?
[01:36] P01: uh, you know, [silence 6s] I was focused on the world uhm itself, the streets and the people. My friend [name] told me it's the same in other games.
[02:12] Interviewer: Q4. Was there any HUD element that didn't work the way you expected?
[02:17] P01: you know, like, the prompts were easy to miss like, without the other stuff. I usually stream as [username] so I play a lot.
[02:42] Interviewer: Q5. How aware were you of the passing of time while playing?
[02:46] P01: you know, um, it felt long when I was lost, I kept checking uh, how long it had been.
[03:16] Interviewer: Q6. Was there a point where you had to stop to figure out what the game was telling you?
[03:22] P01: um, uhm yes, I had to stop um, many times and open the full map. My friend [name] told me it's the same in other games.
[03:53] Interviewer: Q7. What information, if any, did you feel was missing from the screen?
[04:00] P01: like, you know, [silence 3s] I wanted the minimap back, and the objective distance. I usually stream as [username] so I play a lot.
[04:24] Interviewer: Q8. What would you change about the HUD you just used, and why?
[04:29] P01: you know, uhm I would add a small compass so I ahh, do not get lost but keep it clean.
